knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) Give one continuous explanatory example. (2) Give one categorical factor example. (3) What does an interaction term allow between them or among factors?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Continuous e.g. age; factor e.g. territory levels; interaction allows effect of one variable to depend on the level/value of another.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Rating: continuous age x and factor region (levels North/South). (1) Write a linear predictor that includes region as a factor (baseline North) and an age×region interaction. (2) Refuse: 'Add all interactions by default' and 'an interaction is just another main-effect slope.'
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) η = β₀ + β₁x + β₂ I_South + β₃ x·I_South (North baseline). (2) Refuse: include an interaction when theory or evidence says the effect of X depends on another factor. An interaction changes the age slope by region; it is not merely another additive main effect, and defaults are not a warrant.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Adding every interaction by default, or treating an interaction as just another main effect.
